significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the specific conclusion that, in successful encoded jailbreaks, "decoding happens in later layers, after the refusal decision has been made," and that moving the refusal check after decoding causally restores refusal; this is a form-(iii) ordering between measurable computations combined with a form-(ii) causal intervention. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon—the decode-then-answer gap across several encoding classes—and a mechanism that fixes expectations about layer ordering and explains why the model can understand and comply without refusing; this is more constraining than the generic capability-safety mismatch discussed by Wei et al. (2023) and behavioral cipher failures demonstrated in CipherChat (Yuan et al., 2024). The negative branch would distinguishably rule out refusal-before-decode as the common explanation, although it would not resolve alternative mechanisms or other jailbreak families. Topic substitution would not retain this score: generic mechanistic LLM-safety work merits only the topic median, while the claim-specific temporal ordering and its causal consequence justify a higher score.

reach.justification: The transferable handle is the proposed "late-layer refusal re-check" that reads a "post-decode representation"; it is an ex-ante intervention because it can block compliance after internal decoding but before harmful output is emitted. After per-model re-extraction, the claim predicts a substantive relation—decoded harmful meaning should become legible later than the ordinary refusal decision on successful cipher attacks—rather than merely supplying an open-ended procedure for finding some direction. Its asserted scope covers Base64, leetspeak, and ciphers and could inform model auditors or deployment engineers, though the admitted "model-dependent layer structure" and encodings that decode early limit transfer to all architectures and attacks. The topic-substitution check lowers no credit here: mechanistic safety alone supplies no deployment handle, whereas this claim specifically supplies an output-preempting re-check and timing diagnostic.
